S.FORM: pai, kinemnemanga tiamadju tu kemacu tua ljigim nua kakinan.
S.TRANSL: Now, they decided to take their mother's sewing needles.

W.TRANSL: discourse filler, indicating a new topic
decided or thought of, actor focus
sewing needles or box of sewing needles

S.FORM: pai, inika makakiqadilj tia marekaka tua kipaula tua culjan.
S.TRANSL: Now, the two brothers can no longer take the suffering and hunger.

W.TRANSL: discourse filler, indicating change of topic
tolerate, bear. The root isqadilj'bear, tolerate'.
subject case marker for people, plural

S.FORM: pai, paquzipanga nua kina a kaka a tjaljaljak tua kama niamadju.
S.TRANSL: It comes to that they are raised by aunt, their father's younger sister.

W.TRANSL: it comes to that, a discourse filler
to raise, feed. The root isquzip'feed, raise', -anga'change of state'.
GEN, marking the agent of the action

S.FORM: pai

W.TRANSL: look, thereupon, filler to initiate a new topic

S.FORM: pai, samalji a ku salasaladj tua patjara mavuca a caucau.
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, my classmates are curious about blind people.

W.TRANSL: look, thereupon, filler to initiate a new topic
to be surprise, actor focus. The root ismalji'different, weird, special'.
partners, friends, classmates, colleagues. The root issaladj'partner'in RED which indicates plural.
blind, actor focus.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root isvuca'blind, cannot see'.

S.FORM: namadraudraw aken a kemacu tua ku bintu. pai numayan tjakanauanga ku bintu.
S.TRANSL: I forgot to bring my lunch box. come, in that case, let's eat my lunch box.

S.FORM: bulai a vaik itjen a ljemangui? bulai aravac. pai, ari vaiki.
S.TRANSL: Is it a good idea that we go swimming? That's very good. Come, let's go.

S.FORM: qemudjaljanga. inika aken a nakemacu tua kausua. maqati aken a supasedjaman? ita a ku kausua. pai, kadjadjalani a kiljaung.
S.TRANSL: It's raining now. I did not bring an umbrella. Can you lend me yours? I only have one umbrella. Come, let's share the umbrella.

W.TRANSL: it is raining already, actor focus. The root isqudjalj'rain'.
you lend. The root issedjam'borrow, lend'.
I am not sure about this word.

S.FORM: aicu djukap nua vavui. pai, aicu avan a djaladjalan nua vavui.
S.TRANSL: This is the footprints of wild boars. So, this is the path of wild boars.

W.TRANSL: little trail or path. The root isdjalan'road' in RED, smaller road.

S.FORM: pai, iljavaranu. anemanema kudamunu i Taiwan?
S.TRANSL: Come, tell. What fruits are there in Taiwan?

S.FORM: vuvu vavayan, ti kuliu 'a ti paljai amen. pai, suqeljevi amen.
S.TRANSL: Grandma, it's kuliu and paljai. Please open the door for us.

W.TRANSL: subjet case marker for specific noun
subjet case marker for specific noun
you open the door, imperative inclusive, agent of a Paiwan NAF clause. The root isqeljev'open the door'.
we, 1st person PL Nom, patient of a Paiwan NAF clause

S.FORM: pai, qiladju. anema su'anen?
S.TRANSL: Come, sit down. What will you have?

W.TRANSL: sit, imperative exclusive. The root isqiladj- 'sit, seat'.

S.FORM: pai, kusualapav a dengec i tua su mudingan.
S.TRANSL: Come, let me get the crumbs off your face.

S.FORM: pai, kipapaulingavu. akumayanga sa su tjengez?
S.TRANSL: Come on, get it all together. Why are you dozing off like this?

W.TRANSL: be careful, watch out, keep alert. The root islingav'time, wisdom, hurry'.
for what, why. I think this is a combination of aku 'why',maya'like this or similar', and -anga'suffix indicating change of state'.

S.FORM: pai, mayanan maya penurpur a su kaka.
S.TRANSL: Do not yet disturb your brother.

W.TRANSL: disturb, actor voice. The root ispurpur'annoy, disturb'.

S.FORM: pai, maya manu seman-neka-aravac tua zuma.
S.TRANSL: Do not act like so disrespectful to other people.

W.TRANSL: to excessively disregard or disrespect too much, literally to make nothing out of at all. Interesting word!

S.FORM: pai, kiumalju. semiaq sa su sikudan.
S.TRANSL: Come, change to a new leaf. What you did is shameful.

W.TRANSL: be shameful, actor voice. The root issiaq'shame'.

S.FORM: ljaljeqeljeqel aicu a kinsa. pai, seljecuanan.
S.TRANSL: The food is already cold. Go, heat it.

W.TRANSL: cold, in RED. The root is ljaljeqel 'cold'.
this. I always thinkaicuisa-icu; however, Professor Anna Chang said it isaicu, and in Paiwan demonstratives and case marker are "mutually exclusive" (Chang, 1992, p. 88).
heat the food.seljecu'heat food by steam'.

S.FORM: pai, pasazalemani a remasudj tua tjakinepel a qavai. ulja tjen a kemeljang tu pidanga supu a penuljat.
S.TRANSL: Come, let's put all long rice cakes in line on the floor. We want to know how many there are in total.

W.TRANSL: let's place on the floor, imperative, inclusive. The root iszaleman'floor'.
to make peace. It means to arrange or line up the rice cakes in a good way.
know, actor focus. The root is keljang

S.FORM: pai, kesau tua tjacengelj.
S.TRANSL: Go make our lunch.

W.TRANSL: cook, imperative, exclusive. The root iskesa'cook'.

S.FORM: pai, capau azua vasa.
S.TRANSL: Go roast those taros.

W.TRANSL: roast or bake, imperative, exclusive. The root iscapa'roast, bake'.

S.FORM: pai, senasenayu. masepelj itjen.
S.TRANSL: Come, sing a song. We are bored.

W.TRANSL: sing, imperative for the hearer. The root issenay'sing, song' in RED; -u'imperative marker excluding the speaker'.
to be bored.ma- 'to be in the condition of without volition'; the root issepelj'play around without a purpose'.

S.FORM: pai, maya qemaluvu a tja kinateveteveljan.
S.TRANSL: Come on, do not disturb our gathering.

W.TRANSL: mix up or distrub, actor focus. The root isqaluvu'to mix up, distrub'.

S.FORM: maya masepelj a siqunu ni su vuvu, aya aken tjanusun. inika sun a lemang(e)da. pai, mavuciqanga a su lima.
S.TRANSL: I told you not to play wioth your grandpa's small knife. You didn't listen. Look, your hand is cut.

W.TRANSL: play with or fiddle with. The root issepelj'tease, fool around with without purpose'.
small knife usually used by elders to cut betel nuts apart and add lime
listen or hear, actor focus. The root islang(e)da'listen, hear'.
gets cut.ma- 'to be in the state of, without volition'; the root isvuciq'cut, sever'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: maljenguaqanga aza kuang, pai?
S.TRANSL: That gun is ready, right?

W.TRANSL: to already go in the diretion of well.ma- 'to be in the state of without volition';lje- 'to go in the direction of'; the root isnguaq'well'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: inika sun narukisasusu tua mareka tjakaka, pai sipavai tua zuma a hiu niamadju.
S.TRANSL: You did not take good care of our brothers and sisters, therefore they gave their votes to others.

W.TRANSL: to have often cared for.na- 'PRF';ru- 'frequently';kisasusu'to investigate, to look after' with the root issusu'meaning'.
our brother and sister.tja- 'our, 1st person PL GEN clitic';kaka'brother or sister'.
therefore, consequently, but also can mean look in this context.
vote, must be a loanword since in Paiwan there is no phoneme /h/ but I do not know its origin.

S.FORM: saqetju a ku kaka, manusika inika kasikakituluan.
S.TRANSL: My brother is ill, therefore he did not go to school

W.TRANSL: to the school. kakituluan 'the place to learn' with the roottulu'learn, teach'.

S.FORM: pai manasika a i taiwan mavan a ku qinaljan, uta aya aken.
S.TRANSL: Therefore, Taiwan is my home, so I also say.

S.FORM: naminseg a ljavek, ayatua neka nu vali.
S.TRANSL: The sea has calmed down because there is no wind.

W.TRANSL: have become calm.na- 'PRF'; the root isminseg'calm, still'.
? Usuallynuis your (2nd personal plural GEN). Here why the elder saysnuis unknown to me.

S.FORM: kipaula aravac tiamadju ta icu a qudjalj, ayatua siniqaljudj a quma.
S.TRANSL: They suffer severely from this rain, because the farm was washed away.

W.TRANSL: suffer from or experience something bad or encounter.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root ispaula'diaster, pity, experience'.
because or as, provides not the cause but result.
to be swept or washed away. The root isqaljudj'swept or washed away'.

S.FORM: ayatua a picul a ligu nisunanga a penuljat a kemasi tucu a patje palalautanga. amin.
S.TRANSL: Because power, honor, all belongs to you, from now until forever. amen.

W.TRANSL: of yours already.ni- 'of, GEN marker'; -sun'you, 2nd person SING clitic'; -anga'change of state COS'.
forever or everlasting. The root ispalalaut'forever'.

S.FORM: inianga kapazangal a kemesa tucu, ayatua izuanga a tinku.
S.TRANSL: Because of electrical rice cooker, it is no longer difficult to cook now.

W.TRANSL: no longer.ini- 'no, not, NEG'; -anga'marker of change of state'.
electric rice cooker, loanword from Mandarin.

S.FORM: ayatua a benuru uri si'atarivak na 'u lingalingaw.
S.TRANSL: Because exercise will make my body healthy.

W.TRANSL: exercise or do sports or literally to play with a ball, AF. The root isburu'ball', loanword.
to make healthy, IF. The root istarivak'healthy'.

S.FORM: djaljepan a kisasusu aravac tjajuaken a nia sinsi, manu seljaseljang ni kama kisansinsi.
S.TRANSL: So that's why my teacher cares very much for me, because he was dad's colleague at school.

W.TRANSL: so that's the way it is; so the reason why...is that...
our, often used in Paiwan even for its singular sense
to be a teacher, teaching at a school

S.FORM: djaljepan tu kemavasun tua bulabulay, avan susikabulay.
S.TRANSL: Oh, the reason why you are so beautiful is because of the clothes you're wearing!

W.TRANSL: so that's the way it is; so the reason why...is that...
you wear, AF. The root iskava'shirt, clothes'; -sun'you, clitic'.
the way you use to become beautiful or the reason why you become beautiful, IF

S.FORM: sedjaljepsun a kisankalaingan.
S.TRANSL: You are suitable for leadership.

W.TRANSL: you are right or suitable for or you have the quality of.se- 'have the quality of'; the root isdjaljep'fit, suitable, assistant'; -sun'you, 2nd person SIN clitic'.
to become a leader.kisan(e)- 'to become or to act as';kalaingan'the elderest, leader' comes fromka-laing-anwith the rootlaing'the elderest, supervise, leadership'.

S.FORM: a kisedjaljep a mayatucusun a makinamalji?
S.TRANSL: Is it appropriate for you to get so mad like this?

W.TRANSL: to be suitable or appropriate. The root isdjaljep'fit, suitable, assistant'.
to be angry.ma- 'to be in the state of without volition';ki- 'to get or obtain';na- 'PRF'; the root ismalji'different, special, angry or mad'.

S.FORM: uri venli aken tu drusa a djaljeng a nigi. izua a tjelu a djaljeng imaza. nisunaianga a penuljat.
S.TRANSL: I want to buy two bunches of green onions. There are three bundles here. They are all yours.

W.TRANSL: buy, AF. The root isveli'buy or sell'.
binding for flowers or hays or leafy vegetables
binding for flowers or hays or leafy vegetables
of yours, yours already.nisun'your, 2nd person GEN'; -ai- 'LIG,iis probably an extra phone to link with the nexta'; -anga'the change of state COS'.
all for... . The root ispuljat'the meaning of all'.

S.FORM: tadjaljeng azua qarizang.
S.TRANSL: That is a handful/bundle/sheaf of yardlong beans.

W.TRANSL: one bundle, one sheaf. The root isdjaljeng'binding (as for flowers, hay)'.

S.FORM: djemaljeng aken tua ravuc.
S.TRANSL: I am binding thatch.

W.TRANSL: bind, AF. The root isdjaljeng'binding (as for flowers, hay)'.

S.FORM: madjadjaljdjalj amen ka ti kaka i selep.
S.TRANSL: I am next to (subsequent to) selep in the ranking of siblings. I am are youner than selep. [selep is the eldest, and I am the second-born.]

W.TRANSL: to be younger than.ma- 'to be in the condition of';dja- '?'; the root isdjaljdjalj'be second'.
we, 1st person PL NOM. However, the translation goes with the singular 'I'. I did not change amen to aken, knowing Paiwan has a tendency of using the plural form 'we' to indicate collectivity.
I am not sure why here the elder sayskarather thantaas inPaiwan Every Day 629djaljdjalj.
subjet case marker for specific person

S.FORM: djaljdjalj ti uni ta marekakaka.
S.TRANSL: uni is the second among the siblings.

W.TRANSL: subject case marker for specific person

S.FORM: djaljawu! kadjaljawu! kadjaljawi! medjaljaw papedjaljaw lja kadjaljawan
S.TRANSL: Hurry up!You do it more quickly!Let's do it quickly!to become quickerto cause sth to become quicker(house or family name)

W.TRANSL: quick, imperative for the hearer. The root isdjaljaw'fast, speedy'; -u'imperative end case marker for the hearer only'.
You do it quickly.ka- 'used as an inchoative marker'.
We do it quickly.-i'imperative end case marker for the speaker and the hearer'.
to become quicker.me- 'used as agent marker for certain verbs, usually involving change of status'.
to cause something to become quicker.pa- 'to cause to be, usually does not involve secondary agent';pe- 'to emerge, come into view'.

S.FORM: djaljaw angata nu mekelj timadju.
S.TRANSL: He is really fast when he runs.

W.TRANSL: he or she, 3rd person SIN NOM

S.FORM: tjadjaljaw a makahikuki tua makagungkang.
S.TRANSL: Flying is faster than taking a ship

W.TRANSL: to go by plane or fly.maka-'to go by or via'; the root ishikuki'airplane', loanword.
take a ship. The root isgungkang'ship', loanword; the southern Paiwan dialect hasvarukur.

S.FORM: pida 'uyulj a su kinikasiv?
S.TRANSL: How many bundles of wood do you have?

W.TRANSL: subject case marker for conmon NP

your, 2nd person SIN GEN. I write it separately from the next word kinikasiv because the lexicon stands on its own with full meaning in this sentence. When it is part of inflection of a verb, I write it together with the inflected verb to indicate its clitic nature, e.g.su-s<in>i-talem'planted by you or that which you planted'.
literally wood that is collected, undergoer focus because of the infix -in-.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root iskasiv'wood'.

S.FORM: caljeqil aravac azua kinakasikasivan.
S.TRANSL: That wood fiber is very hard.

W.TRANSL: wood fiber or literally the character or property that is made of wood, undergoer focus. The root iskasiv'tree'; -an'nominalization'.

S.FORM: kasikasiven aravac azua i kavulungan.
S.TRANSL: There in Mount kavuliungan, it is filled with pristine forest.

W.TRANSL: foresty, filled with forest, RED and PF. The root iskasiv'wood, tree'; -en'patient focus'.
Mount kavulungan, the sacred Paiwan ground.ka...an'principal or prototypical manifestation of'; the root isvulung'elder'.

S.FORM: inika makaya a maqudjalj a pukasivan.
S.TRANSL: The place where the woods are cannot catch rain.

W.TRANSL: to become wet because of rain. The root isqudjalj'rain'.
the place which has the woods.pu- 'to have'; the root iskasiv'tree'; -an'location marker'.

S.FORM: neka nu kasiw i tjumaq.
S.TRANSL: There is no wood [for burning] in the house.

S.FORM: kakudralananga a kasiw a kusinitalem kakakedrian aken
S.TRANSL: The tree I planted when I was young has grown really bigger/taller.

W.TRANSL: to have become bigger or to have grown.ka...an'principal manifestation of'; the root iskudral'big'; -anga'change of state, COS'.
planted by me, undergoer voice.ku-'my, 1st person SIN GEN';si- 'instrument focus'; the root istalem'to plant or grow'.

S.FORM: kalemedep aken, madjadjas an ngaci.
S.TRANSL: As soon as I dive in, I accidentally catch mussels.

W.TRANSL: dive or sink in, AF.ka- 'inchoative marker'; the root isledep'sink, dive'.
catch.ma- 'to be in condition of without own volition'; the root isdjadjas'hold, entrust'.

? As far as the syntax goes, I think it should be the oblique casetaortua. However, the recording sounds likean. Could it bema-djadjas-anwith the LOC marker? I am not sure. I don't know how to explain this.

S.FORM: nakidjadjas ti kama tua paljing.
S.TRANSL: Father grasped the door.

W.TRANSL: held on tight or grasped or grapplied.na- 'PRF';ki- 'get, obtain'; the root isdjadjas'take, hold, entrust'.
subject case marker for human being

S.FORM: kusipadjadjas a sausi nua 'umaq ta kuqali.
S.TRANSL: I give the key of the house to my friend.

W.TRANSL: I give.ku- 'my, 1st person SIN GEN clitic';si- 'IF';pa- 'to cause to be'; the root isdjadjas'take, hold, entrust'.
my friend. The root isqali'friend, male friend'.

S.FORM: djadjasu azua turivecan.
S.TRANSL: Take that tool.

W.TRANSL: take or grab, imperative for the hearer. The root isdjadjas'take, hold, entrust'; -u'imperative end marking only for the hearer'.
that or those. a 'subject case marker for common noun'; the root is zua 'that, those'.

S.FORM: inika aken a padjadjas a paqeteleng tua paisu.
S.TRANSL: I do not entrust my money to anyone casually.

W.TRANSL: entrust.pa- 'to cause to be or occur'; the root isdjadjas'take, entrust'.

S.FORM: nadjemadjas a ku kaka tua vurasi.
S.TRANSL: My sister has sweet potatoes.

W.TRANSL: to have holden or have had, AV.na- 'PRF'; the root isdjadjas'hold, have, entrust'.

S.FORM: nusauni pusaladjuanga a qemarut ta aljualju.
S.TRANSL: In a while you help giving away the candies.

W.TRANSL: you help.pusaladj'help, literally to have partner or friend'; -u'IMP, for the hearer'; -anga'COS'.
share, distribute, give away, AV. The root isqarut'share'.

S.FORM: nu qemaruqarut itjen tua nemanga, nakuya inika papamamaw.
S.TRANSL: When we alloting or distributing things, it is not good to not give the same [it is bad to be unfair].

W.TRANSL: being sharing or alloting, AV. The root isqarut'distribute, share, allot'.
to make the same. The root ismamaw'the same'.

S.FORM: qarutu ta mareka a sinsi aicu a kamaya.
S.TRANSL: Please send these mangoes to every teacher.

W.TRANSL: you send, imperative for the hearer. -u'IMP mareker'; the root isqarut'distribute, send'.

S.FORM: siqarut a viduat na takec tua mamazangiljan.
S.TRANSL: Give the share of the ribs of the Reeves's muntjac to the chief.

W.TRANSL: to give away or share.si- 'IF'; the root isqarut'things that are distributed'.

S.FORM: nu naqemudjalj, vaik aken a ljemulju tua ngacingaci.
S.TRANSL: If it rains, I will go collecting snails.

W.TRANSL: it has rained, AV.na- 'PRF'; the root isqudjalj'rain'.
collect or pick up or find, AV. The root isljulju'pick up'.
snails. The root isngaci, RED implies plural, synonymous withlulianddingding.

S.FORM: tjasikamanguaq aravac a lamug.
S.TRANSL: Flour is very good for our body.

W.TRANSL: to be beneficial to us, UV.tja- 'our, 1st person PL GEN';si- 'IF'; the root isnguaq'good, well'.
flour. Synonyms includdimpung, loanword from Minnan, which is only seen in Ferrell, andundungku, loanword from Japanese.

S.FORM: dikiru aken.
S.TRANSL: I can do it.

S.FORM: dikiru timadju a pacun.
S.TRANSL: He can see.

W.TRANSL: he or she, 3rd person SIG NOM

S.FORM: maya ljiadet tua sapui, maculjusun.
S.TRANSL: Do not go near the fire, you will be burnt.

W.TRANSL: get near. The root isdet'proximity, nearness'.
to get warm or burnt. The root isculju'heat, warmth'; -sun'you, 2nd person SIN, postclitic'.

S.FORM: mapadetanga aravac a tja masalut.
S.TRANSL: Harvest festival is just around the corner.

W.TRANSL: to be made very close already, or just around the corner. The root isdet'proximity, close'; -anga'change of state'.
our, 1st person PL GEN. tja 'our' is used a lot in Paiwan language to indicate a sense of community without the need of translating the genitive form.

S.FORM: madadet aravac azua nu sinitalem a kasiw.
S.TRANSL: Those trees you planted are too crowded. [Semantic subject is ERGATIVE].

W.TRANSL: too close to each other or crowded, AV. The root isdet'proximity, closeness'.
your, 2nd person PL GEN, used as the subject of the UV verb that follows sinitalem.
used to be planted, UV. The root istalem'plant'.

S.FORM: tjadedet a paqulid a nu pinarecunguljanan.
S.TRANSL: Your blood relation is really closer. [You are really closer in blood relation.]

W.TRANSL: closer.tja- 'comparative case'; the root isdet'near, close, proximity'.
blood relation. The root iscunguljan'relatiive'. This is a near synonym withpinarekakakakakanin Paiwan Every Day 598.

S.FORM: dedet anan a tja pinarekakakakakan.
S.TRANSL: We are close relatives.

W.TRANSL: sisterhood or brother-hood. The root iskaka'brother or sister'. This is a very interesting word, complicated in the way it is formed and richer in the production of its meaning. However, I can't analyze it right now. My apology. I will do it next time.

S.FORM: pacaingan a gung a pidedet.
S.TRANSL: Tie the cow nearby.

W.TRANSL: to make tied. The root iscaing'to join, to fasten'.
cow or ox, loanword from Minnan.
close by. The root isdet'proximity, nearby'.

S.FORM: padetanga paqulid a kaljauragan.
S.TRANSL: Fall is indeed already around the corner.

W.TRANSL: to arrive, to be nearby or around the corner.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root isdet'close by'; -anga'COS'.
indeed, really. The root isqulid'true, sincere, genuine'.

S.FORM: idedet a nia qinaljan a kemasi maza.
S.TRANSL: Our village is close from this place. [Our village is nearby.]

W.TRANSL: in proximity or nearby.i'LOC'; the root is de-det, du-dut, dung-dung'close by; nearby'.

S.FORM: dungdung a sema yubingkiuku a kemasi tjanuamen.
S.TRANSL: It is close to go to the post office from our place.

W.TRANSL: close to, proximity, nearby place, synonymous withdudutordedet.
with us, towards us, our place, depending on the context

S.FORM: namaduduangasun?
S.TRANSL: Are you mad? [Have you been in the state of anger?]

W.TRANSL: are you mad? na- 'PRF'; ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root is dudu 'anger, mad'; -anga 'COS'; -sun 'you, 2nd person SIN clitic'.

S.FORM: nakeman ta puduku a kakanen timadju, kirimu, vaikan a papucemel.
S.TRANSL: He ate poisonous food. Hurry up, send him to the doctor.

W.TRANSL: has eaten, AV.na- 'PRF'; the root iskan'eat'.
poisonous, to have poison.pu- 'get, obtain'; the root isduku'poison', loanword from Japanese.
he or she, 3rd person SIN NOM
let's go. I have yet to study the marker -an; it seems much more complex than we now know of.
to be made to get the medicine.pa- 'to make happen'; -pu-'to get, obtain'; the root iscemel'medicine, grass'.

S.FORM: izua 'u taiday a qadupu a valjitjuq, sa 'ivalit a'en.
S.TRANSL: I have a 100-dollar bill, and I want to change.

S.FORM: nu qivu itjen, nakuya a masiduduan.
S.TRANSL: When we speak, it is not good to carry anger.

W.TRANSL: it is bad to or it is not good to. The root iskuya'bad luck, misfortune'.
carry anger.masi-'carry, transport' (Ferrell, p. 25); the root isdudu'anger, mad'; -an'nominalization'.

S.FORM: kinaduduan aken ni kina tasauni.
S.TRANSL: Just now I was really scolded by mom.

W.TRANSL: be scolded, UV.ka...an'principal, main; prototypical manifestation of' (Ferrell, p. 18); the root isdudu'anger, mad'.

S.FORM: anema su kudain a kikadudu tjai tja'ma?
S.TRANSL: What are you doing, pissing off our dad like that?

W.TRANSL: thing done. The root iskuda'what, rule, work'; -in'perfecive marker; action already begun or accomplished; object or product of past action'(Ferrell, p. 17).

If we usemalimormadraudraw, the main part of the utterance will bemadjeleanga a malim/madraudrawtuangadan nua caucau. This word also breaks a previously established phonological rule which says Paiwan languages avoids vowel clusters.maalim,madjeleangaare two examples. You hear clearly how two vowels stand next to each other.

S.FORM: maretimaljimaljianga a quljaw na alay tucu.
S.TRANSL: Nowadays threads have different colors. [Literally: Now the color of threads is already different.]

W.TRANSL: to have become different. The root ismalji'different, special' in RED; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: naseminamalji a caquan nua kumakuma a semankaljualaq.
S.TRANSL: Spiders are suprisingly talented in making webs. [Literally: Spiders' web-making talent is amazing.]

W.TRANSL: suprising or amazing, AV. The root ismalji'different, special'. What issina? Could it besi-na'to be used for, IF', giving two na in one word?
talent. The root iscaqu'be able to, capable of'; -an'nominalization NMZ'.
spider. Ferrell hadljualaqas 'spider' (p.56), but nowkumakumaandcacagaljare more common.
make webs, AV. The root isalaq, tolju-alaq'spider', toka-ljualaq'spider's web'.aray nua kumakumais another expression for spider's web.

S.FORM: alapen a nia paisu na cemakacakaw.
S.TRANSL: A thief stole our money. [Literally: Our money was stolen by a thief.]

W.TRANSL: stolen, UV.(m)a- 'to be in the condition of'; the root islap'take, replace'; -en'UV case marker'.
money, loanword from Spanish peso, which travelled to Taiwan from the Philippines.
of GEN, which in a Paiwan UV sentence serves as the case marker for the actor
the one who steals, a thief, AV. The root iscakaw'steal, stolen'.gurucuki, a loanword, also means a thief, though I have no idea where it came from asthiefin Japanese is 泥棒 どろぼう?

S.FORM: kipualang aken tua zikang.
S.TRANSL: I'll find out what time it is.

W.TRANSL: to get understanding or knowledge of, to find out.ki- 'to get or obtain';pu- 'to have'; the root isalang.
I, 1st person singular NOM clitic, but I put it separately.
time, loanword from Japanese 時間 じかん.milinganis another word for time.

S.FORM: saladji. pasaladji. saladji a kemim.
S.TRANSL: No, I don't want to. No, I don't want to. Forget i, don't bother trying to find it.

S.FORM: pualjuan nusauni a vava.
S.TRANSL: Add sugar to the liquor later.

W.TRANSL: to make something a place with sugar, to add sugar to, UV.pu- 'to get or obtain'; the root isalju'sugar, sweet'; -an'NMZ'.
subject case marker NOM in Paiwan, but it is the object in meaning.

S.FORM: nguanguaq aravac a nu qata.
S.TRANSL: Your glass beads are very pretty.

W.TRANSL: pretty. The root isnguaq'good, well' in RED for emphasis of degree.

S.FORM: navaik ti kama tatiyaw a kipucemel tua aljis.
S.TRANSL: Dad went to get medicine for the teech [see the dentist] yesterday.

W.TRANSL: to get medicine or to see a doctor.ki- 'to get or obtain';pu- 'to have'; the root iscemel'grass, herbal medicine'.

S.FORM: pinaka tua ngadan ni yisu kiristu a inuli, amen.
S.TRANSL: In Jesus Christ's name we pray, amen.

W.TRANSL: through or in the name of
pray, loanword from Japanese 祈る いのる. Ferrell (1982) has this wordkialjing(rootaljing) as 'pray'. However, nowadaysinuliorkiqaungor 'iquangis more common in the church context.

S.FORM: akuken a samalji tua su sikudan.
S.TRANSL: I am surprised at your behaviour.

W.TRANSL: feel surprised. The root isalji'undefined' (Ferrell, p. 55).
behavior, deed, doing. The root iskuda'work, regulation'.

S.FORM: mapida mareka a su aljak?
S.TRANSL: How many kids do you have?

S.FORM: alapu tua sialja sa sevalji a su kaka.
S.TRANSL: Take that baby wrap and carry your sister on the back.

W.TRANSL: take, imperative end case marker. The root islap'take, replace'.
that used for carrying, IF.si- 'IF'; the root isalja'undefined' (Ferrell, p. 54)
carry on the back, imperative. The root issevalj'carry on the back'.
younger or elder brother or sister

S.FORM: tiaken a navaik a ma ripun. akusun a kemeljang tjanuaken?
S.TRANSL: It was I who went o Japan. Why do you know me?

W.TRANSL: I, NOM.ti'case marker for person, proclitic'; the root isaken'I' orken'I' withabeing 'LIG?'. In Ferrell (1982) and ILRDF Online Paiwan Dictionary,akenis split intoa-kenwith the rootkenand a 'undefined'. I've never consideredkena root. This is new to me.
to have been to or went to.na- 'PRF'; the root isvaik'go, come'.
towards, to. This may be a word with a lost root or prefix with the meaing of direction. I have not found any source to support this yet.
why do you.aku'why';sun'you, 2nd person singular NOM, clitic'.
know, AV. The root is keljang 'knowledge, understanding'.

S.FORM: ainu a kaus? ku sikaus ta siyaw. inu a ‘u sivecivecik?
S.TRANSL: Where is the soup spoon? I use it to serve soup. Where is my pen? ainu or inu: wherea: subject case markerkaus: ladle, soup spoonku or ‘u: my, 1st person singular GENsi-kaus: to use the ladle to get soup. The root is kaus 'ladle'. ta: OBLsiyaw or siav: soupsi-veci-vecik: thing used for w

W.TRANSL: to use the ladle to get soup. The root iskaus'ladle'.
thing used for writing, pen.si- 'IF'; the root isvecik'writing, pattern' in RED

S.FORM: aiyanga, ‘u singelitan tjanusun.
S.TRANSL: Oh my, how I miss you!

W.TRANSL: the state of missing or thinking of, NMZ. The root issingelitorsinglit'to miss, to think of'; -an 'nominalization NMZ'.
towards you, about you, 2nd person singular and plural OBL

S.TRANSL: In the past herding cattles was considered a taboo. na-p<en>alisi: to have been forbidden or regarded as a taboo, AV. The root is palisi 'taboo'. tua: OBLpa-quzip: herd or feed. pa- 'to cause to be'; the root is quzip 'herd, nurture' used for animal and human being. gung: cow, cattle, lo

W.TRANSL: to have been forbidden or regarded as a taboo, AV. The root ispalisi'taboo'.
herd or feed.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root isquzip'herd, nurture' used for animal and human being.

S.FORM: namadjuq a ku ljinay i qaqeregan.
S.TRANSL: My umbrella was left in the room.

W.TRANSL: umbrella. A synonymkausua, loanword from Minnan, is also used.

S.FORM: ruadjuadjum a vakela.
S.TRANSL: Arrow is usually sharp.

W.TRANSL: sharp.ru- 'be frequently/habitually'; the root isadjum'sharp point' in RED.

S.FORM: aicu a cakar namasan kakituluan nua mimaqacuvucuvungan a uqaljaqaljay.
S.TRANSL: This men's house has become the school of young men who are turning into adults.

W.TRANSL: men's house, a meeting place for young and adult men
the place of instruction or school.ka--an'the main or principal place';ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root istulu'instruct, teach'.
to become adults, AV.mi- 'agent marker';ma- 'to be in the condition of';qa- orka- 'inchoative marker'; the root iscuvung'adult, complete, enough' in RED for present progressive.
men. The root is uqaljay 'boy, man' in RED for plural.

S.FORM: kiljivakan a mareka qayaqayam.
S.TRANSL: Love every species of bird.

W.TRANSL: to have love, UV. The agent of this UV verb is missing but can be understood as we all. Can-anbe the third imperative end case marker in addition to-iand-u? In what circumstances does a Paiwan UV omit its subject? These are interesting questions to investigate.
subject case marker for NOM, which in a Paiwan UV sentence refers to the object.
each and every.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root isreka'each, everyone'.

S.FORM: sannguaq a ada.
S.TRANSL: Onion is delicious.

W.TRANSL: tasty, delcious. The root isnguaq'good, well'.

onion in RF (1982). ILRDF Online Paiwan Dictionary does not have this word; instead, it hascanga, a loanword from Minnantshang-á. And in "List of Southern Pawian Vocabulary", there isada'onion' or 'scallion'. Another more common word isnigifor scallion andtamanigifor onion. Both are loanwords from Japanese ねぎ and 玉ねぎ たまねぎ.

S.FORM: abunai aravac a sapui. gemagalj aravac azua a djalan.
S.TRANSL: Fire is very dangerous. That road is very dangerous.

W.TRANSL: dangerous, fearful, AV. The root isgagalj'fear, danger'.

S.FORM: nu temulutulu a vavuluvulungan, naljiabar a tjacalinga a lemangdangda.
S.TRANSL: If the elders are teaching, we open our ears and listen.

W.TRANSL: be teaching, AV. The root istulu'teach, instruct' in RED for present progressive.
elders. The root isvulung'old, senior' in RED for plural.

to have already open ears.na- 'PRF'; lji- '?'; the root isabar'earlobe' in RF (1982). I didn't find it in ILRDF Online Paiwan Dictionary nor List of A Thousand Paiwan Vocabulary. The common word for ear is calinga. It will be interesting to pursue the meaning and use of words likeabar. They stay in a conjugated form while the root form is already lost.
listen, AV. The root islangda'listen' in RED for emphasis.

S.FORM: liyaw a talem ni kama a abar (yasi).
S.TRANSL: The coconut trees planted by father are a lot. (Father plants many coconut trees).

W.TRANSL: plant, cultivate, UV. Also considered a root form; this is the first word I find that in root form, it is in undergoer voice or patient focus.
of, GEN, used to bring the subject or actor of the UV verb.

S.FORM: nananguaqan aravac a mareka tia Pia.
S.TRANSL: Pia and those with him, everyone is very nice.

W.TRANSL: kind, nice, have good virtues. The root isnguaq'good, blessed'.
subject case marker for plural.ti- 'subject case marker for person';-a'pluralizer with personal pronouns and pronominal article' (RF, 1982).

S.FORM: kemakan a aljak.
S.TRANSL: The kid is eating. k<em>a-kan: eating, AV. The root is kan 'eat'. a: subject case marker. RF (1982) defined, 'equational construction marker for noun phrase'. aljak: kid, child

W.TRANSL: subject case marker. RF (1982) defined, 'equational construction marker for noun phrase'.

S.FORM: ‘a 2005 a cavilj pasemalaw a sihu tua sivecikan nua kacalisiyan na kai. pai, avananga a tjavecik a patje tucu. sa pakakacui a vecik nua i kiukai ‘atua siniljaui nua sihu, sa avananga a maseljuseljudj tucu tua semanvavecikan tua tjakai a sepaiwan.
S.TRANSL: In 2005 the government announced the writing systems of indigenous languages. Look, they have become our writing systems until now. And they integrated the system used in the church and announced by the government, and they have been used now for the making of the written literature for us Paiwan p

W.TRANSL: government, loanword from Japanese 政府 せいふ.
that which is used for writing or writing system.si- 'IF'; the root isvecik'writing, drawing, pattern'; -an'nominalization NMZ'.
our writing.tja- 'our, 1st person plural GEN proclitic'.
church, loanword from Japanese 教会きょうかい.
announced or made, UV. I cannot find the root of this word.
government, loanword from Japanese 政府 せいふ.
to have been used or kept for. I cannot find the root of this word.

make the written literature, AV.seman- 'make, manufacture';va- 'frozen prefix with unclear meaning'; the root isvecik'writing'; -an'NMZ'.pinavavecikanis used as contract; literally in Paiwan the word means that which is put in the writing, UV.

S.FORM: ‘a patagitagilj a ta semansisiu ‘ata sambika a kasi i casaw a mareka rutjaucikecikel, sinivecik tua kai nua sepaiwan tu sikamadjuluan nua vecik ta kai, sa ‘ivavadaqan tua ramaljemaljeng, sa patagilj a semanvecik tua tjakai. pai, a kinateveteveljan na kiukai namasanpazangal aravac ta tjakinitulu tua tjakai a sepaiwan.
S.TRANSL: Every missionary that came from outside started to make the Bible and hymns. The Paiwan language was written down, in order that the written language is easy to understand, they asked elders and started to make the writing of our language. Now, the meeting in the church has become a very important place for our instruction of our Paiwan language.

W.TRANSL: in the beginning or start to. The root istagilj'start' in RED.
missionary or teacher. The root istjaucikel'story' in RED.
used as written word, UV and IF. The root isvecik'writing, pattern, drawing'.
in order that, complementary. This is also an interesting functional word.
to make something easy to understand, UV.si- 'IF';ka-an'principal, main';ma- 'to be in the condition of, agent marker'; the root isdjulu'easy'.
our language.tja'our, 1st person plural GEN prolitic';kai'language'.
meeting or congregation. The root istevelj'meet, gather' in RED.
church, loanword from Japanese 教会きょうかい.
our instruction, UV. The root istulu'teach'.
our language.tja'our, 1st person plural GEN prolitic';kai'language'.

S.FORM: masatemulu tua sinzia, pai ‘ a i 1951 izua rutjaucikecikel a kemasi ingeris a bukesi a ti yuhani, sinkauljan a pasa ta qinaljan nua sepaiwan. ‘ itulu timadju tua kai na pinaiwanan, sa pusaladj a ‘ emumalj tua pinaiwanan a sisiu ‘atua sambika, sa a patagiljanga a vencik tua pinaiwanan a kai.
S.TRANSL: In order to teach believers, see, in 1952, there was a pastor and missionary, yuuhani (Reverend John Whitehorn), from England,. he was sent to the villages of the Paiwan people. He studied the Paiwan language, and helped to change (translate) the Bible and hymns to the Paiwan language, and this began the writing of the Paiwan language.

W.TRANSL: to be able to teach, AV.ma- and <em> 'AV marker';sa- 'wish to'; the root istulu'teach'.
believer, loanword from Japanese 信者 しんじゃ.
someone in the habit of teaching or missionary. The root istjaucikel'story, reason'.
come from, AV. The root iskasi'to be from, come from'.
pastor, loanword from Japanese 牧師 ボクシ.
to be sent to. The root issekaulj'serve, to be a missionary of'.
helped or assisted with.pu- 'to obtain';saladj'companion, partner'.

change, i.e. translate, AV. The root isumalj- 'change, alter'. This is interesting phonologically. When a Paiwan word begins with a verb, the AV form starts withm- likem-alap'to take', but this one starts with the infix <em>. It is reasonable to think there must be a glottal /q/or /k/or /‘/before the infix because infix does not stand in the beginning of a word. Therefore, I added the glottal.
Bible, loanword from Japanese 聖書 せいしょ.
hymns or praise songs, loanword from Japanese 賛美歌 さんびか.
it started already. The root is tagilj 'start'; -anga'COS'.

S.TRANSL: Since the year of 1945, believers of the Christian Presbyterian churchstarted to arrive at the Paiwan villages. Because there were very many people who believed, and the church soon grew very fast.

W.TRANSL: indicating a time in past, case marker?
come, arrive, AV.ma-'to be in the condition of'; the root isngetjez'come'.
believers, loanword from Japanese信者しんじゃ.
Paiwan people.se- 'belonging to or coming from a certain place'.
start, for the first time, in the beginning.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root istagilj'start, beginning'.
a lot of, used for people
believe, AV. The root issalu'faith, believe, thank'.

S.FORM: amin a vecik a pasemalaw tua pasasevalivalit, tua penacalivatan na taqaljaqaljan, a papacun tua natemalidu a kakudan nua kacalisiyan, sa tuluwan, sa pazurungan. ljakua neka nu vecik tua kai nua kacalisiyan.
S.TRANSL: There is only pattern,with which to tell the changes, the history of fellow villagers,to show the impressive part of the indigenous culture, and its instruction, and its continuance. However, there is no written language for indigenous peoples.

W.TRANSL: to or for the purpose of, LIG
changes.pa- 'to cause to be';sa- andse- 'have the quality of'; the root isvalit'change, replacement' in RED
things that have passed or history, UV. The root iscalivat'pass over'; -an'nominalization'.
to show or present. The root iscun'see'.
exciting or interesting or impressive, AV.na- 'have become'; the root istalidu'appreciate, spectacular'.
continuance or transmission.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root iszurung'push forward'; -an'NMZ'.
this is also very interesting case marker to think further about. Is it a demonstrative for Paiwan? I see it many times functioning as demonstrative before a noun.

S.FORM: ljakua a kacalisiyan i Taiwan, kemasicuai amin a tjaucikel, amin a vecik, a pitua inalang a kasiw, a qaciljai, katua vincikan a itung, a inalang a cempu, a vincikan i ta lima.
S.TRANSL: But for indigenous peoples in Taiwan, for a long time, there is only oral story, only patternas per patterns made on the tree trunk, on the stone, and drawn on clothing, drawn in weaving, written on the hand.

W.TRANSL: hill people or indigenous people. The root iscalisi'hill, slope'; -an'specific location in space, referent focus, NMZ'.
coming for a long time ago, AV.kasi'come from';cuai'a long time ago'.
made, UV. The root islang'make';malangmeans to make, AV. The vowel /a/ must be an addition to make the word pronounciable, likelapandm-a-lap'take, AV'.
the thing that is drawn or pattern, UV. The root isvecik'pattern'; /e/ disappears phonologically.
made, UV. The root islang'make';malangmeans to make, AV. The vowel /a/ must be an addition to make the word pronounciable, likelapandm-a-lap'take, AV'.
weave, AV. The root iscepu'weaving'; /e/ disappears phonologically.
the thing that is drawn or pattern, UV. The root isvecik'pattern'; /e/ disappears phonologically.

S.FORM: namasan ljuqes, vavak nua i naqinaljanan. sa a tjakai mavan napakeljangan tua tjakakudakudan a i qinaljan.
S.TRANSL: It [Language] is the essence and soul of a people. Our language is the means through which we present our culture in the indigenous village.

W.TRANSL: people of a village.na-'of, belonging to, GEN'; the root isqinaljan'village'; -an'specific location in space, referent focus'.
our (spoken) language.tja- 'our, GEN, proclitic';kai'language, spoken word'.
to make known or reveal or present.pa- 'to cause to occur'; the root iskeljang'know, understand'; -an'reference focus'.
our ways of life or our culture.ka- 'inchoative marker'; the root iskuda'custom'; -an'NZM'. [Now I am getting curious about-an. This suffix is used a lot and has many functions or meanings.]

S.FORM: a kai nua caucau sinipavai nua cemas, a napakisumalji a manguaqan, tjasipakakeljakeljangan tua tjavarung.
S.TRANSL: Human language is a gift from God, a very special blessing, the means through which we reveal our heart.

W.TRANSL: given, UV.si- 'IF';pa- 'to cause to be'; the root isvai'give, offer'.
different or special.na- 'PRF';pa- 'to cause to be';ki- 'to get, obtain';su- '?'; the root ismalji'different'.
blessing, NVZ.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root isnguaq'good, well'; -an'nominalization'.

used by us to make known or to show, IF.tja- 'our, GEN, proclitic, used as the agent of IF sentence';si- 'IF';pa- 'to cause to be';ka- 'inchoative marker'; the root iskeljang'know, understand' in RED; -an'referent focus'. [This word is complicated. A Paiwan word is a sentence. Can there be two focuses in one Paiwan word? Can this word combine UV and IF?]
our heart. The root is varung 'heart'.

S.FORM: nu ini'anga kaminasinasi a caucau a qemuzimuzip, tjasannamacaiyanga.
S.TRANSL: If a person or an animal is no longer breathing, we think they died already.

W.TRANSL: is breathing, AV.ka-'inchoative';mi- 'anget marker'; the root isnasi'breath' in RED
we consider dead.tja- 'our';san- 'construct';na-'PRF';ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root iscai'death'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: pazangal a cuai itjen i ta zaljum a inika minasi.
S.TRANSL: It is difficult for us to stay in the water for a long time and not breathe.

W.TRANSL: to breathe, AV.mi- 'agent marker for certain verbs, usually intransitive'; the root isnasi'life, breath'.

S.FORM: aicu a maqesang a caucau, nakuya a sinasi nimadju.
S.TRANSL: He or she who has asthma has a weak respitory system.

W.TRANSL: this.a'subject case marker'; the root isicu'this, these'.
cough, in extension asthma.ma- 'to be in the condition of, AV'; the root isqesang'cough'.
bad, poor, weak. The root iskuya'bad'.
thing or organ used for breathing, respitory system, UV. The root isnasi'breath, life'.
his or her, 3rd person singular GEN

S.FORM: punasi tua nguanguaq.
S.TRANSL: Be given a blessed life.

W.TRANSL: to get life or to obtain life.pu- 'get or obtain'; the root isnasi'life'.
good or well. The root is nguaq 'good, well' in RED.

S.FORM: nekanga nu tjapazangal tua tjanasi.
S.TRANSL: Nothing is more valuable than our life.

W.TRANSL: nothing, no more. The root isneka'no, not'; -anga'COS'.
more important or valuable.tja- 'comparative, prefix';pa- 'to cause to be'; the root iszangal'value, importance'.
our life, our breath.tja- 'our, 1st person plural GEN, prolitic'; the main word isnasi'life'.

S.FORM: liaw a sacemel i gemaduan.
S.TRANSL: The mountain area is filled with game.

W.TRANSL: mountain area. The root isgadu'mountain'; -an'nominalization of location'. I am not so sure about the semantic difference betweengemaduanandgaduorgadugadu. I have not found an example yet. Hopefully will do one day.

S.FORM: djuljam aya itjen tua uqaljay nu mapana izua inalap, nu magadu izua qinaljup.

to be in the river or to go to the river. The root ispana'river'.
catches or gains, UV. Literally, it means things that are caught. The root islap'take, catch'.
to be in the mountains or to go to the mountains. The root isgadu'mountain'.

game, UV. Literally, it means things that are hunted. The root isqaljup'hunt, hunting area'.qaljupis also a noun, meaning the leaves of Miscanthus or Chinese silvergrass used as the wrapping of sticky rice or millet.

S.FORM: i gadugadu a nia umaq. valivali nu kaljaculjuwan.
S.TRANSL: Our house is on the hill. It is cool in summer.

W.TRANSL: hill. The root isgadu'mountain' in RED, used to indicate decrease in size.
house.uma'is also heard in sinvaudjan paiwan.
to have breeze or wind. The root isvali'wind' in RED, used to indicate a continuous movement of wind of lesser strength or scale.
summer.kalja...an'time characterized by something'; the root isculju'heat'.

S.FORM: inika nanguaq a mikemudan itjen.
S.TRANSL: It's not good to boast about ourselves.

W.TRANSL: good or well. The root isnguaq'good, well'.
to boast about or to act arrogant.

S.FORM: makudakuda a kakaveliyan nu sa kava?
S.TRANSL: How much is this piece of clothing?

W.TRANSL: how much, for value or price. The root iskuda'what'. In my dialect sinvaudjan Paiwan, we use 'pida'.

price. The root isveli'buy, sell, trade'. Morphologically, I think the combination has two steps:ka-veli-anand thenka-kavelian. The firstka- is 'inchoative marker', and the secondka- is unclear. -anis NMZ (nominalization). Needs more data to compare and confirm.

S.FORM: pakananguaq amen a mapuljat tua su sikudaan.

all.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root ispuljat'all, every'.
behavior, style, how one conducts him- or herself. The root iskuda'custom, way of being'. The vowels 'a' in this case do not merge.

S.FORM: anema kudakudain niamadju i pukukan?
S.TRANSL: What are they doing in the chicken farm?

W.TRANSL: activity or doing, UV. The root iskuda'what'.
chicken farm or henhouse.pu- 'to have'; the root iskuka'chicken'; -an'localization'.

S.FORM: maya kinemenem tua kitjukuda tua su cekelj.
S.TRANSL: Do not think of leaving your spouse.

W.TRANSL: think or or plan. The root isnemnem'think, plan'.
divorce or departure from.ki-tju-'to do or use separately'; the root iskuda'what'. The word becomes a noun through nominalization; a synonym iskitjuvaday.

S.FORM: maretimaljimalji a kinakemudan na zua mareka kisi.

S.FORM: ari vaiki a pacun ta iga.
S.TRANSL: Come, let's go watch movies.

W.TRANSL: let's go. The root isvaik'go, come';-i'end case marker for imperative, inclusive (INCL)'.
watch.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root iscun'see'.
movies, loanword from Japanese 映画 えいが.

S.FORM: aicu a kadjunangan imaza rukacunuq aravac.
S.TRANSL: The land here is quite prone to collapse.

W.TRANSL: collapses easily or often.ru- 'frequent, habitual';ka- 'stative'; the root iscunuq'landslide, collapse'.

S.FORM: tima a uri cemunuq tua aicu a djeljep?
S.TRANSL: Who is going to collapse this wall?

W.TRANSL: wants to or be going to
collapse, actor voice (AV). The root iscunuq'landslide, collapse'.
wall. In the dialect of southern Paiwan,kabi'loanword from Japanese かべ 壁' is also used.

S.FORM: azua gadu a tja pacucunan macunucunuq sakamaya.
S.TRANSL: That mountain we are looking at keeps collapsing.

W.TRANSL: is collapsing or sliding. The root iscunuq'landslide, collapse'.

S.FORM: kamacunuq a gadu i palikulikuz tua qinaljan, tjuruvu a nasepacevelj.
S.TRANSL: When the mountain behind the village collapsed into a landslide, many were buried alive.

W.TRANSL: collapsed or cumbled, actor voice (AV). The root iscunuq'landslide, collapse'.
behind, in the back of. The root islikuz'back' in reduplication (RED).
to have been buried. The root iscevelj'bury'.

S.FORM: kacunuqan tasauni a nia puljuangan ta zua qudjalj kata vali.
S.TRANSL: Our cowshed was just washed away by landslide caused by rain and wind.

W.TRANSL: to be washed away by landslide. The root iscunuq'landslide, collapse'.
just now, a while ago. A synonym iskasauni.
cowshed.pu- 'to get, obtain'; the root isljuang'cow'; -an'nominalization (NMZ) of location'.

S.FORM: macunuq a niamadju a umaq ta luni.
S.TRANSL: Their house collapsed because of earthquake.

S.FORM: naremekutj a cunuq i pasa kavulungan.
S.TRANSL: The landslide in Mount kavulungan is terrible.

W.TRANSL: to have been scary or terrible, actor voice (AV). The root isrekutj'fear, awed'.nareminkutjis used in Northern Paiwan.
towards or near the point of

S.FORM: qinceng a mareka nakuyakuya a pakatua palisi nua malada.
S.TRANSL: Evil spritis are all blocked outside by the sacrificial ritual the priest performs.

W.TRANSL: is blocked, undergoer voice (UV) indicating passive. The root isqeceng'stop, block'.
evil or bad spirit. The root iskuya'bad, ill, misfortunte' in reduplication (RED).
through, as a result of, due to

S.FORM: qecengen a zaljum nua caucau, saka masan vacalj.
S.TRANSL: People block the water, and it becomes a deep pool.

W.TRANSL: block, undergoer voice (UV) indicating passive. The root isqeceng'stop, block'.
of, genitive (GEN) case marker. In Paiwan, the actor of a UV sentence is in GEN.
become.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root issan- 'to be elected as, to make to become'.

S.FORM: maqeceng amen tua cunuq.
S.TRANSL: We are blocked by landslide.

W.TRANSL: to be stopped or blocked.ma- 'to be affected by, without volition'; the root isqeceng'stop, block'.

S.FORM: qemeceng a kisacu i sakinting tua inika kacalisiyan.
S.TRANSL: The police stops non-indigenous people at the checkpoint.

W.TRANSL: stop, actor voice (AV). The root isqeceng'stop, block'.
police, loanword from Japanese けいさつ警察.
check point. I think this is a combination of Paiwan prefixsa- 'in direction of' and Japanese loanword てんけん点検.
hill people or indigenous people. The root iscalisi'hill, slope'.

S.FORM: naparamur a nia djeli.
S.TRANSL: We were all smiles.

W.TRANSL: to have been a lot of or excessive.na- 'perfective (PRF); the root isparamur'over, excessive'.

S.FORM: djemelidjeli timadju tua levan.
S.TRANSL: She is smiling with joy.

W.TRANSL: she or he, 3rd person singular nominative (NOM)
joy, happiness. The root isleva'pleasure, happiness, award'; -an'nominalization (Nmz) case marker'.

S.FORM: nakuya semandjeli tua zuma a caucau.
S.TRANSL: It is not nice to laugh at other people.

W.TRANSL: bad or not good. The root iskuya'bad, ill, unfortunate'.
to laugh at or make fun of.seman- 'make, manufacture'; the root isdjeli'smile, laugh'.

S.FORM: a su sikaivuan penapedjeli aravac.
S.TRANSL: The way you said it is very funny.

W.TRANSL: to be used in saying or the way something is said.si- 'to be instrument for'; the root isikai'say, speak'.
to make people laugh or be funny, actor voice (AV).pa- 'to cause to be';pe- 'to emerge or come into view'; the root isdjeli'laugh'.

S.FORM: qemuma a sengsengan ni kama. ljemita a qadav masengsengseng sakamaya. qucengelanga ti kama tua sikipaqadavan. metjevenanga a itung tua zengzengan. ljakua, tucu a cavilj liaw a kiniqinuman ni kama a vaqu. djemeli ti kama tua levan.
S.TRANSL: Father makes a living out of farming. He always works every day. Father's skin is tanned and dark. His clothese is wet becaue of sweat. But. this year Father has a great millet harvest. Father laughes with joy.

S.FORM: nasecugcug tua tulaku a sema kalingu a kisia.
S.TRANSL: A train bound for Hualien collided unexpectedly with a truck.

W.TRANSL: to have collided with or hit.na- 'perfective (PRF)';se- 'occur suddenly or unexpectedly'; the root iscugcug'collide, strike'.
truck, loaword from Japanese トラック.
train, loanword from Japanese きしゃ.

S.FORM: aicu a kikasiw masa mavananga a seman qaqumain.
S.TRANSL: This act of cutting trees is for the purpose of making farm.

W.TRANSL: cut or fell trees.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root iskasiw'tree, wood'.
is or equals to. -anga'change of state (COS)'.
to make or manufacturer, actor voice (AV).
farm or land to be cultivated.qa- '?'; the root isquma'field, farm'.

S.FORM: kisamuljau a qemuma tua paketjaw.
S.TRANSL: Work hard to plant peanuts.

W.TRANSL: work hard, as a request to the listener. The root issamulja'envy'; -u'imperative ending'.
plant or cultivate, actor voice (AV). The root isquma'field, farm'.

S.FORM: masanliawliaw a tja qinuman a paiwan, ljakua tjalja namasanparavacan a vaqu.
S.TRANSL: We Paiwan have many agricultural produces, but millet is the most special.

W.TRANSL: to be many or a lot.masan'quantifier'; the root isliaw'many' in reduplication (RED), indicating abundance.
literally that is grown in the farm, i.e. agricultural produces. The root isquma'field, farm'.
to be special.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root isravac'especially, very'.

S.FORM: ari tja pusaladj tjai tja vuvu a semanquma.
S.TRANSL: Come let's help Grandpa with farm work.

W.TRANSL: help.pu- 'to have'; the root issaladj'company, spouse'.
oblique (OBL) case marker, used for people
to make field or farm, actor voice (AV). The root isquma'field, farm'.q<em>umais a synonym. SeePaiwan Every Day 390.

S.FORM: uri kiqinuman amen tua djulis tucu a qiljas.
S.TRANSL: We will harvest red quinoa this month.

W.TRANSL: will or be going to, future.

to harvest farm produce, actor voice (AV).ki- 'to get or obtain';q<in>uma-(a)n'that is produced in the field or farm produce'; the root isquma'field, farm'.vavuais more used in Southern Paiwan when referring to farm.

S.FORM: nakemanangasun tua cemel?
S.TRANSL: Have you taken the meds?

W.TRANSL: have you eaten somthing, actor voice (AV).na- 'perfective (PRF)'; the root iskan'eat'; -anga'change of state'; -sun'you, 2nd person singular nominative (NOM) bound'.

S.FORM: kipucemel nu saqetju itjen.
S.TRANSL: We see a doctor if we feel ill.

W.TRANSL: go get medicine or see a doctor. The root iscemel‘medicine’.

S.FORM: demangadangas ti kama tua cinpu a dradrakuyan.
S.TRANSL: Father is smoothening the edge of the woven basket.

W.TRANSL: is smoothening the edge, actor voice (AV). The root isdangas'edge, cliff' in reduplication (RED) for present contiuous.
subject case marker for specific person
woven product, undergover voice (UV). The root iscepu'weave'.

S.FORM: salialim ti vuvu ta cemepu tua sekam.
S.TRANSL: Grandma is busy weaving straw mat.

W.TRANSL: is busy. The root issalim'busy' in reduplication (RED).maqutjaqutjavis the synonym from Northern Paiwan.
subject case marker for specific person
grandma, grandpa, elder in the village

S.FORM: titjen a paiwan, inika palaing ta uqaljayqaljay kata vavayavayan, kicaquan a mapuljat tua tjemenun.
S.TRANSL: We Paiwan people, regardless of men and women, everyone learns to weave.

W.TRANSL: accord with or adhere to.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root islaing'obey, follow'.
learn.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root iscaqu'knowledge, talent'; -an'referent focus (RF)'.
all, everyone.ma- 'be affected by'; the root ispuljat'all, '.
weave net, actor voice (AV). The root istjenun'weave'.

S.FORM: namayatucu a nia kakudan a kemasicuay.
S.TRANSL: Since in the past our custom was like this.

S.FORM: nu izua a pupalisiyan i qinaljan, izua a qemavaqavay, a venavavava, a cemuljuculju tua dridri.
S.TRANSL: Where there is a festival in the village, there is making of sticky rice cake, brewing of wine, and roasting of pig.

S.FORM: nu izua a nia qaljaqalja a kemasi cadja, sipakikadja a nasanguaq a kakanen.
S.TRANSL: When there are our friends visiting from afar, we treat them with delicious food.

S.FORM: nu namalap a cinunan ta sacemel, pavadis ta mamazangiljan, sa paqarut ta marevetjevetjek, sa naljemavak ta taqaljaqaljan.
S.TRANSL: When a hunter has caught game, he offers the chief's portion to the chief (as tax), and he gives a part to the custodian of the hunting ground, and he shares his game with fellow villagers.

S.FORM: aicu a kinsan ta udung imaza makan aravac.
S.TRANSL: The noodles cooked here is very delicious.

W.TRANSL: this.a- 'subject case marker for commun nouns'; the root isicu'this'.
being cooked, undergoer voice (UV). The root iskesa'cook'.
noodles, loanword from Japanese うどん.
here.i- 'in or at, locative (LOC)'; the root ismaza'here'.
tasty or delicious.ma- 'be in the condition of'; the root iskan'eat'. In southern Paiwan, we saysanguaqmore often.

S.FORM: sikakan aicu a kizing katua qecap.
S.TRANSL: These spoon and chopsticks are used for eating.

W.TRANSL: to use for eating.si- 'instrument focus marker';ka- 'inchoative marker'; the root iskan'eat'.

S.FORM: salialim ti kina ta semankakanen.
S.TRANSL: Mom is busy preparing food.

W.TRANSL: is busy, present contiuous. The root issalim'busy'; the reduplication (RED) form issali-ali-m.
subject case marker for specific person
make or prepare food, actor voice (AV).san- 'construct, work on';kakanen'food' with the rootkan.

S.FORM: tisun a nakemesa tua tja kenamain?
S.TRANSL: Did you make the breakfast?

W.TRANSL: you, 2nd person singular nominative (NOM).ti- 'subject case marker for specific person'; the root issun'you, 2nd person singular'.
cooked, actor voice (AV). The root iskesa'cook'.
our, 1st person plural genitive (GEN), usually bound, but seems also to serve as a general demonstrative.

S.FORM: kemakan ti kaka tua gang.
S.TRANSL: Brother is eating crabs.

W.TRANSL: is eating, actor voice (AV). The root iskan'eat'.
subject case marker for specific person

S.FORM: kanen ni kama azua sinandjamai ni kina.
S.TRANSL: Dad ate the dishes prepared by mom.

W.TRANSL: eat, undergoer voice (UV). The root iskan'eat'.
of, genitive (GEN) case marker, used as the subject case marker of a UV verb.
vegetable cooked by, UV.san- 'to work on'; the root isdjamai'vegetable'.
of, genitive (GEN) case marker, used as the subject case marker of a UV verb.

S.FORM: masan liawliaw a kakanen i suibai.
S.TRANSL: There are many foods in the store.

W.TRANSL: many many. The root isliaw'many' in reduplication (RED).
store, loanword from Japanese しょうばい 商売.

S.FORM: pikeman tua cengelj.
S.TRANSL: Eat a simple lunch.

W.TRANSL: eat simple or informal or casual, actor voice (AV).pi- 'to do at random'; the root iskan'eat'.

S.FORM: kakudan a pakan tua tja pinakasengseng a caucau.
S.TRANSL: It is customary to feed people who work for us.

W.TRANSL: custom, rule. The root iskuda'work, rule, what'.
to make sb. eat or to feed.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root iskan'eat'.
our, 1st person plural genitive (GEN), used as subject of a undergoer voice (UV) verb
work, UV.paka- 'to cause to go'; the root issengseng'work, make'.

S.FORM: uri keman aken ta udung.
S.TRANSL: I will have noodles.

W.TRANSL: eat, actor voice (AV). The root iskan'eat'.
noodles, loanword from Japanese うどん.

S.FORM: makesanga a sinankaiven ni kina. idu, kanianga.
S.TRANSL: Mom has cooked dinner. Come, let's eat.

W.TRANSL: to have been cooked.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root iskesa'cook'; -anga'Change of State (COS)'.
dinner, undergoer voice (UV).san- 'to work on'; the root iskaiven'dinner'.
of, genitive (GEN) case marker for the agent of the UV verb
come. -u'imperative end marker of invitation or request, exclusive'.
let's eat. The root iskan'eat'; -i'imperative end marker of invitation or request, inclusive'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: paday a kinsa ni kina tua tja kaiven tucu.
S.TRANSL: Rice cooked by mother as our dinner tonight. (Mom cooks rice for our dinner tonight.)

W.TRANSL: cooked. A different form iskinesa, where the sound of /e/ is so soft that it seems to disappear.
of, genitive (GEN) case marker as the subject case marker for the agent of an undergoer voice (UV) verb

S.FORM: aicu a tjangetjang makaya tja kesain, makaya tja qavain uta.
S.TRANSL: This pumpkin, we can cook it, we can also make cake with it.

W.TRANSL: this.a'subject case marker'; the root isicu'this, these'.
our, 1st person plural genitive (GEN), used as the agent of a undergover voice (UV) verb
our, 1st person plural genitive (GEN), used as the agent of a undergover voice (UV) verb
make sticky cake, UV. The root isqavai'traditional Paiwan sticky millet cake'.

S.FORM: vaik aken a kisapui a sema tua nia ljaqediqedi a kemesakesanga.
S.TRANSL: I am going to get fire from our neighbor who is cooking at the moment.

W.TRANSL: to get fire.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root issapui'fire'.
is cooking, AV. The root iskesa'cook' in reduplication (RED), which indicates a present continuous.

S.FORM: inu azua nu kakesan?
S.TRANSL: Where is your kitchen?

S.FORM: kanakemesa tu ita vasa katua vaqu, sikavetu nua tacemekeljan.
S.TRANSL: You only need to cook one taro and one millet, you can feed the entire family.

W.TRANSL: to have cooked, actor voice (AV). The root iskesa'cook'.
feed.si- 'be instrument';ka- 'stative'; the root isvetu'full in the stomach'.

S.FORM: kapucekecekeljmun, sepacengceng i taihuku aken.
S.TRANSL: When you were marrying, I happened to be in Taipei. [I was in Taipei on your wedding day].

W.TRANSL: as you were getting married, past.ka- 'in past';pu- 'to get, obtain'; the root iscekelj'spouse' in reduplication (RED);pucekecekelj'getting married, marrying'; -mun'you, 2nd person plural, nominative (NOM), bound'.
happen to be in the condition of.se- 'occur suddenly or unexpectedly';pa- 'to cause, to occur'; the root iscengceng'exactly'.
Taipei, loanword from Japanese たいほく 台北.

S.FORM: pacengceng izua kinsa vasa i kakesan.
S.TRANSL: There happens to be taro rice in the kitchen.

W.TRANSL: happes to be.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root iscengceng'exactly, as luck would have it'.

S.FORM: aicu a paljaqic avan a kakasengsengan a seman langalj.
S.TRANSL: This farges evodia fruit is the principal [wood] material used to make a linking cup.

W.TRANSL: farges evodia fruit, a species of tree

the material to be used for.... The root issengseng'make, manufacture'. Perhaps the word is formed first aska-sengseng(ka- 'inchoative marker that shows the beginning of a process') and second aska-kasengseng-an(ka...anindicates 'main, principal').
linking cup, a traditional cup used in reception or wedding.

S.FORM: aicu ku kinasengseng tasauni.
S.TRANSL: This was what I made just now. [This was my most recent work. / I just made this.]

W.TRANSL: the thing made or work, undergover voice (UV). The root issengseng'make, manufacture'.
just now, just a while ago.kasauniis a synonym. Bothta- orka- are prefixes for past events.

S.FORM: nu pasuvililj ta cengelj, uri vaik aken a masengseng tua lalingedan.
S.TRANSL: I will go make the nose-flute in the afternoon.

W.TRANSL: to make or manufacture, with agent marker. The root is sengseng 'make, manufacture'. A synonym iss<em>an'do or make'.

S.FORM: anema su sengsengan tucu?
S.TRANSL: What is your job now? (What do you do now?)

W.TRANSL: work or job or occupation. The root issengseng'to make or manufacture'.

S.FORM: tima nakitauvalit tua su sengsengan?
S.TRANSL: Who took the place of your work? [Who's your replacement?]

W.TRANSL: to have replace or take the place of. The root isvalit'exchange, replace, ancestor'.
work or job. The root issengseng- 'to make or manufacturer'.

S.FORM: masasevalivalit a zemang tua saqetjuqetju.
S.TRANSL: Take turns to look after the patient.

W.TRANSL: take turns.ma- 'to be in the condition';sa- 'in the direction of';se- 'have the quality of'; the root isvalit'exchange, replace, ancestor' in reduplication (RED)
take care of, look after, or keep company, actor voice (AV). The root iszang'look after, keep company'.
patient or the person that is hurting. The root issaqetju'hurt' in RED.

S.FORM: pinavalitan azua namapalak dinki na djalan.
S.TRANSL: Those broken streetlights have been replaced.

W.TRANSL: to be replaced, undergoer voice (UV). The root isvalit'exchange, replace, ancestor'.
that have been broken. The root ispalak'damage, hurt'. A synomyn isna-malje-kuya'damaged' with the rootkuya'bad'.
light, loanword from Japanese でんき 電気.

S.FORM: uri vaik aken a sema gingu a kivalit tua taidaidai a paisu.
S.TRANSL: I am going to the bank to exchange for 100-dollar bills.

W.TRANSL: be going to or will, future.
go to or towards, actor voice (AV).
bank, loanword from Japanese ぎんこう 銀行.
exchange.ki- 'to get, to obtain'; the root isvalit'exchange, replace, ancestor'.

S.FORM: napavalit sun tua su migami? ui, napavalit aken tua vaquan a migami.
S.TRANSL: Have you changed your eye-glasses? Yes, I've changed to a new pair of eye-glasses.

W.TRANSL: to have changed.na- 'perfective (PRF)';pa- 'to cause to occur'; the root isvalit'change, replace, ancestor'.
eye-glass, loanword from Janapese めがね メガネ 眼鏡.
to have changed.na- 'perfective (PRF)';pa- 'to cause to occur'; the root isvalit'change, replace, ancestor'.
eye-glass, loanword from Janapese めがね メガネ 眼鏡.

S.FORM: uri semupu aken, sa mayanan a galugu.
S.TRANSL: I want to read, so do not yet make noise.

W.TRANSL: to read, actor voice (AV). The root issupu'read'.
do not yet.maya'do not, prohibition';anan'yet, still'.mayananalso means 'wait for a moment' when used by itself, which is related to the meaning of 'not yet'.

S.FORM: uri kivangalj amen tua manges tu kedri.
S.TRANSL: We are going to pick a few mangoes.

W.TRANSL: pick up fruit.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root isvangalj'fruit'.

S.FORM: navenangalj a nia saviki tucu a cavilj.
S.TRANSL: Our betel nut trees have produced fruits this year.

W.TRANSL: to have produce fruit, actor voice (AV).na- 'perfective (PRF)'; the root isvangalj'fruit'.

S.FORM: nekanan nu vangalj na aicu a kasiw.
S.TRANSL: This tree has not yet fruited.

S.FORM: kakedrian anan a’en, nakemaizuanan a’en i spungudan.
S.TRANSL: When I was a child, I lived in spungudan.

W.TRANSL: Damei Village Mudan Township Pingtung Taiwan, a very small Paiwan village of around 50-80 households.

S.FORM: venava ti vuvu tua sikasalut.
S.TRANSL: Grandma makes wine for the harvest festival.

W.TRANSL: make wine, actor voice (AV). The root isvava'wine'.
subject case marker for specific people
for the harvest festival. The root issalut 'a festival for harvest, to thank ancestors'.

S.FORM: masanliawliaw a tjavangavang kasicuaian.
S.TRANSL: Our toys were many in the past. [We had many toys in the past.]

W.TRANSL: there were many.masan“quantifier for countable nouns”; the root isliaw“many” in reduplication (RED)
our toys.tja- “our”, bound; the root isvangavang“toys”.
in the past. The root iscuai“long ago”.

S.FORM: anema a ’u ikain?
S.TRANSL: What shall I say?

S.FORM: nakuya untingting sa padingwawa.
S.TRANSL: It’s not good to be driving and then calling on the phone.

W.TRANSL: it is not good to (do something)
driving. The root isunting‘drive’, loanword from Japanese うんてん 運転.
to call on the phone. The root isdingwa‘telephone’, loanword from Minnan.

S.FORM: masengac timadju a kiqaqivuan tjanusun.
S.TRANSL: She dislikes talking to you.

W.TRANSL: dislike or hate, actor voice (AV).ma- 'to be affected by without volition'; the root issengac'dislike'.
speak with or talk with. The root isqivu'speak, narrate, so say'. Conjugation of the word is interesting, but I will leave this exercise until later.

S.FORM: semengac a kai nimadju, namaya uta a kinudan nimadju.
S.TRANSL: His words are disgusting, the same also with his deeds.

W.TRANSL: to disgust or loathsome, actor voice (AV). The root issengac'disgust, dislike'.
his or her, 3rd person singular genitive (GEN)
his or her, 3rd person singular genitive (GEN)

S.FORM: nu izua nasaqetju i tjumaq, palisi ti vuvu a vavayan tua tjasevalitan.
S.TRANSL: When there is a sick one at home, Grandma prays to our ancestors.

W.TRANSL: subject case marker for specific person
our ancestors.tja- 'our, 1st person plural genitive (GEN)', bound;sevalit-an'ancestor' (rootsevalit'change, replace').

S.FORM: anema a saqetjuan ni kama i cekaw?
S.TRANSL: What is the illness of Uncle cekaw?

W.TRANSL: disease, illness. The root issaqetju'hurt, injured'.

S.FORM: pupicul a su kininemeneman.
S.TRANSL: Your thought is powerful.

W.TRANSL: powerful or to have strength.pu- 'to have'; the root ispicul'power, strength'.

S.FORM: masalu ta su papupicul tjanuamen.
S.TRANSL: Thank you for encouraging us.

W.TRANSL: to make to have power or encourage.pa- 'to cause to happen';pu- 'to have'; the root ispicul'power'.
towards us or to us. The root isamen'we'.

S.FORM: mipicul a sikataqaljan a kitulu tua sikipaisuan.
S.TRANSL: Fellow people are working hard to learn about making money.

W.TRANSL: work hard or strive. The root ispicul'strength, power'.
people of the same indigenous village
learn. The root is tulu 'learn, study'.
the way to get obtain. The root is paisu 'money'.

S.FORM: namaquyu ti sinsi.
S.TRANSL: Teacher did not get enough sleep.

W.TRANSL: have not had enough sleep.na- 'perfective (PRF)';ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root isquyu'not enough sleep'.
subject case marker for specific person
teacher, loanword from Japanese 先生 せんせい.

S.FORM: mavilad a sema ta qinaljan niamadju.
S.TRANSL: He ran away towards his village.

W.TRANSL: run away or escape. The root isvilad'escape, disperse'.
their, 3rd personal plural genitive (GEN). Though plural, it can also be used for singular case.

S.FORM: vaik amen a pusau tua qaljaqalja.
S.TRANSL: We are going to see our guests out.

W.TRANSL: to show sb. to the door, to see sb. out
guests or visitors. The root isqalja'visitor, enemy' in reduplication (RED)

S.FORM: aicu a sinzia pakatua inuli a kipaparangez tua cemas.
S.TRANSL: Such is a disciple that puts his trust in God in prayer.

W.TRANSL: believer, follower, disciple, loanword from Japanese しんじゃ.
prayer, loanword from Japanese 祈り いのり.

her or his, 3rd person singular genitive (GEN)

S.FORM: sinivai ni kina aicu a ku nasi i tua ku pinualjakan.

W.TRANSL: gave, undergoer voice (UV).si- 'be cause/instrument of'; the root isvai'give, offer as gift'.
genitive (GEN) case marker, used as the subject of a UV verb
birthday (UV).pu- 'to have'; the root isaljak'child'; -an'abstract state nominalization'.

S.FORM: natemalidu aravac a kinateveteveljan nu maljeveq.

meeting or get-together or party. The root istevelj'assemble, meet' in reduplication (RED).

S.FORM: migacalj a'en i tja pitju a milingan nu kadjamadjaman.

morning in reduplication (RED). The root isdjama'dawn'.

his or her, 3rd person singular genitive (GEN)

work or job. The root issengseng'make, manufacture'; -an'abstract state nominalization'.

S.FORM: temeljar a qiljas tucu a qezemezemetj.

he or she, 3rd person singular nominative (NOM)
returns, actor voice (AV). The root iscikel'return, get back together'.

S.FORM: ljaljeqel a kadjunangan tasauni. tekelu ta linalja.
S.TRANSL: It is very cold today. Drink warm water.

boiled water. The root islalja- 'boiling water'; -in- 'undergoer voice (UV) case marker'.

S.TRANSL: I am going to buy piegon pea, sweet potato, taro, millet and meat.

S.FORM: tucu tjuruvuanga a kakedrian a sekacalisian sinipualjak sa uqacanga i lizuk.
S.TRANSL: Now, there are already many indigenous children born and growing up in the city.

kid or children. The root iskedri'small, young'.
indigenous or people from the hill. The root iscalisi'hill, slope'.
born. The root isaljak'kid, child';pu- 'to have';pu-aljak'to give birth', actor voice (AV);-in-'undergoer voice (UV) case marker';s<in>i-pu-aljak'to be born' (UV).
growing up. The root isqaca'big';u- 'UV case marker'? Grow up in AV form ismeqaca.
plains or city or urban area

S.FORM: kicauvu ta kaitungan aya ti kina, ayatua ljaljeqel aravac.

subject case marker for a specific person

socks. Also read and written askucusta, loanword from Japanese くつした. Note the middle /cu/ and /s/ are merged in my mom's use of the word.

S.FORM: nakuya inika itjen a pasusu tua siuntinting a kakudan, maqaluvu a tja djalan.

follow or obey. The root issusu‘meaning’.
to use (as instrument) for driving. The root isunting‘drive’ in reduplication (RED), loanword from Japanese 運転うんてん.
custom or ways of doing things. The root iskuda‘rule’.

family. The root iscekelj'spouse, family, relative'.

our, 1st person plural genitive (GEN). Here it is used as the subject of the undergoer voice (UV) verb.

have fun or play.ki- 'to get something'; the root isvangavang'fun, child play'.
bored.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root issepelj'tease for fun'.

so said or say in this way

selfish. The root isqilji'selfishness' in reduplication (RED) for stress.

to have passed.ka- 'in past in variation withta-';se- 'to have quality of'; the root isparia'pass or qualified'.
university, loanword from Japanese だいがく大学.

have fee sored.na- 'perfective' (PFV);ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root isngilu'exhaustion, tiredness'.

hiking or mountain climbing. The root isgadu'hill, mountain'.
hobby or the thing that you like to do. The root issaljinga'envy, parade'.

become adult.ma- 'to be in the condition without volition';qa- orka- 'stative gerundivization'; the root iscuvung'enough' in reduplication (RED).

your, 2nd person genitive (GEN), used as the subject or agent of a UV verb
gave, undergoer voice (UV).si- 'to be instrument or cause of';pa- 'to cause to be'; the root isvai'give, send'.

dance, actor voice (AV). The root iszian'dance'.
